summary: This is a well-documented, artifact-backed preregistered paired evaluation of a bounded Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) intervention for intent→configuration NetOps. Execution artifacts show a degenerate null outcome (every generated candidate passed the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11=240, no discordant pairs). The study is scientifically useful as an archival, reproducible accounting of a preregistered run, but the manuscript currently emphasizes provenance bookkeeping over conventional scholarly exposition and omits some concise disclosures and presentation elements needed to make the scientific contribution clear to conference reviewers/readers. Several resolvable clarifications and manuscript edits are required before this can be finalized for publication.
critical_issues: Prespecified primary comparison (GVR vs schema-constrained baseline, C vs B) listed in the preregistration was not executed and no rationale is recorded in the archived artifacts; the manuscript must explicitly label this as a prespecified-but-unexecuted comparison and not imply it was performed.

The preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation, but the executed design used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one generation per task reused across arms). This invalidates the preregistered power arguments for the executed run and must be made unambiguous in Methods, Abstract, and Conclusion.—the manuscript currently acknowledges this but the descriptions are scattered and insufficiently explicit for readers.

The manuscript reads heavily as provenance/inventory rather than a concise, literature-grounded scientific paper. Key elements required by standard conference prose are missing or buried (clear evidence-to-claim mapping, nearest-work comparison matrix, and a compact method description of the actual executed pairing/generation semantics).

The statistical analysis is degenerate because of zero discordant pairs; the paper must not present hypothesis-test results without making plain that no within-pair information exists to estimate effect size under executed semantics, and that the paired p-value/CI are deterministic consequences of the contingency. Although this is discussed in artifacts, the manuscript presentation must make the inferential limits explicit and prominent.
required_revisions: Explicitly state in the Abstract and Methods that the prespecified (C vs B) comparison was not executed and that no recorded rationale appears in the archive; revise any language that might be read to imply that both prespecified primary comparisons were performed. (Resolvable from archived execution/preregistration artifacts.)

Consolidate and prominently restate the executed design (shared_initial_candidate semantics): include a brief, plain-language Methods subparagraph that states 'one shared initial generation per task was reused across arms (model_calls_used=240), maximum 1 repair attempt per task, deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 used for scoring' and cite the exact archived artifact paths/SHA256s already in the bundle. (Resolvable from execution_manifest and model_configuration artifacts.)

Replace or compress provenance-heavy blocks with conventional scholarly prose: add a one-page evidence-to-claim table (compact) mapping each principal claim to the specific archived artifact(s) (paths and SHA256). Include a nearest-work comparison matrix (1/2 page) that places this run relative to closest prior GVR/validator NetOps studies. All content can be constructed from the supplied verified bibliography and manuscript_evidence_bundle. (Resolvable from the provided evidence and citation records.)

Revise Results and Statistical Interpretation to make an explicit, standalone paragraph that (a) explains why n11=240 and zero discordant pairs render the paired estimate degenerate, (b) states that the McNemar p=1.00 and bootstrap CI=[0.0,0.0] are deterministic consequences of the observed contingency under the preregistered analysis executor, and (c) links this degeneracy directly to the shared-generation semantics and the invalidated power assumption. (Resolvable from analysis_results and deterministic_reconciliation artifacts.)

Add an explicit short subsection (Methods or Limitations) listing the exact preregistration→execution deviations (shared-generation vs preregistered independent generation; unexecuted C vs B comparison), and state how each deviation affects inference. If no recorded operational rationale exists for an unexecuted prespecified item, state that fact plainly rather than implying a rationale. (Resolvable from preregistration and execution artifacts.)
optional_revisions: Move full provenance inventory (long lists of artifact paths/hashes) into a short 'Artifact appendix' paragraph or referenced archived manifest, and keep the main paper narrative focused on methods, results, interpretation, limitations, and implications (to satisfy normal conference prose expectations).

Expand the discussion of verifier-completeness risk using concrete examples from the archived task/generator pairs (e.g., show a representative task manifest entry and the validator trace as an inline illustrative snippet) to make construct-validity concerns more tangible for readers. (These examples exist in the archive.)

Where space permits, add a small table listing per-cluster acceptance rates and sample difficulty metadata (already present in execution/task_manifest.jsonl) to support the claim that all clusters showed 100% acceptance.

Add a brief, explicit 'How to reproduce' checklist (3–6 bullet items) that points to the archived files for deterministic reruns (task manifest, RNG seeds, adapter configuration, model configuration), so other researchers can immediately re-run the alternative independent-generation design using the supplied artifacts.
